questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:
1. The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were part of the original Preamble adopted in 1949.
2. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. The Preamble can be amended under Article 368, provided the basic structure is not destroyed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), so statement 1 is wrong. Kesavananda Bharati overruled the earlier Berubari view and held the Preamble is part of the Constitution, which can be amended without altering its basic features.
questions.h: Berubari said NO, Kesavananda said YES

questions.q:
Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship of India may be lost through:
1. Renunciation
2. Termination
3. Deprivation
4. Dismissal from government service
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Act recognises exactly three modes of loss: renunciation (voluntary), termination (on voluntarily acquiring another nationality) and deprivation (compulsory, by the Central Government). Dismissal from service has no bearing on citizenship.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 21A was inserted in the Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
2. Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education to all children in the age group of 6 to 16 years.
3. The 86th Amendment also added a Fundamental Duty on parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their child between 6 and 14 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 21A covers children aged 6 to 14, not 6 to 16, so statement 2 is wrong. The same amendment added Article 51A(k) as a Fundamental Duty and changed Article 45 to early childhood care for children below six.

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State?
questions.e: Article 50 is the Gandhian-liberal Directive aimed at securing the independence of the judiciary at the lower level. Article 40 is about village panchayats, Article 44 about a uniform civil code and Article 48 about agriculture and animal husbandry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ordinances issued by the President under Article 123:
1. An ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.
2. It must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless disapproved earlier.
3. The President cannot withdraw an ordinance once it has been promulgated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The President can withdraw an ordinance at any time, so statement 3 is wrong. The ordinance-making power is a legislative power of the executive and is limited to matters on which Parliament can legislate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a Money Bill:
1. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha can amend a Money Bill and the Lok Sabha is bound to accept the amendment.
3. The decision of the Speaker on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. The Speaker's certificate under Article 110(3) cannot be questioned in any court or in either House.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about writs:
1. Prohibition can be issued only against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities.
2. Quo warranto can be issued against the holder of a private office as well as a public office.
3. Certiorari is issued by a higher court to quash an order already passed by a lower court or tribunal.
4. Habeas corpus can be issued against a private person who has illegally detained someone.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Quo warranto lies only against a substantive public office created by statute or the Constitution, so statement 2 is wrong. Habeas corpus lies against both public authorities and private persons, whereas prohibition is preventive and certiorari is curative.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Part IX-A of the Constitution deals with municipalities.
2. The Eleventh Schedule contains 18 functional items.
3. Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years.
4. The provisions of Part IX automatically apply to the Scheduled Areas without any modification.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Part IX-A (74th Amendment) covers municipalities and Article 243I provides for the five-yearly State Finance Commission. The Eleventh Schedule has 29 items (the Twelfth has 18), and Part IX applies to Scheduled Areas only as extended by Parliament through the PESA Act, 1996.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 after the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
o: It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month by a special majority
It must be approved by both Houses within two months by a simple majority
The President may proclaim it without the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
It lapses automatically after one year unless re-approved
questions.e: The 44th Amendment cut the approval window from two months to one month, required a special majority, and made the Cabinet's written recommendation compulsory. Once approved, an emergency continues for six months and can be extended indefinitely by six-monthly approvals.
questions.h: 44th: one month, special majority, Cabinet in writing

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.e: The NHRC is a statutory body created by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Election Commission (Article 324), Finance Commission (Article 280) and UPSC (Article 315) are provided for directly in the Constitution.

questions.q:
Arrange the following trading companies in the chronological order of their formation:
1. Dutch East India Company
2. English East India Company
3. French East India Company
4. Danish East India Company
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The English Company was chartered in 1600, the Dutch in 1602, the Danish in 1616 and the French (under Colbert) in 1664. The French came last, which is why they were late rivals in the Carnatic.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Cornwallis : Permanent Settlement of Bengal
2. Wellesley : Subsidiary Alliance
3. William Bentinck : Abolition of Sati
4. Canning : Vernacular Press Act
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was passed under Lytton, not Canning, who was Viceroy during the Revolt of 1857. The other three pairs are correct: Permanent Settlement 1793, Subsidiary Alliance from 1798, and Regulation XVII of 1829 against sati.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of leaders and centres of the Revolt of 1857 is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Nana Sahib led the revolt at Kanpur, while Jhansi was the centre of Rani Lakshmibai. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1815.
2. The Prarthana Samaj was founded by Keshab Chandra Sen.
3. Dayananda Saraswati's Satyarth Prakash is the main text of the Arya Samaj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay) was founded by Atmaram Pandurang, with Keshab Chandra Sen's influence, not by Sen himself. Roy's Atmiya Sabha preceded his Brahmo Samaj of 1828.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Dandi March
2. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
3. Poona Pact
4. Second Round Table Conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Dandi March (March 1930), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) and Second Round Table Conference (September to December 1931) came first, and the Poona Pact followed in September 1932 after the Communal Award. The pact is why Gandhi attended the second conference.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946:
1. It accepted the Muslim League's demand for a sovereign Pakistan.
2. It proposed that the Constituent Assembly be elected indirectly by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
3. It proposed a Union to handle defence, foreign affairs and communications.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Mission rejected a separate sovereign Pakistan and instead proposed a three-tier structure of Union, groups of provinces and provinces. The Constituent Assembly was to be elected by the provincial assemblies, not by direct adult franchise.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: Which one of the following Harappan sites has yielded evidence of a ploughed field and fire altars?
questions.e: Kalibangan in Rajasthan shows a pre-Harappan ploughed field with criss-cross furrows and fire altars in the citadel and lower town. Lothal is known for its dockyard and Dholavira for its water-harvesting system.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History I, Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the inscriptions of Ashoka:
1. Most of his inscriptions are in the Prakrit language and the Brahmi script.
2. Some of his inscriptions in the north-west were written in the Kharosthi script.
3. Major Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war.
4. James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in which the edicts are written.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The north-western edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra use Kharosthi, and Prinsep's decipherment of Brahmi in 1837 allowed the edicts to be read.
questions.s: Spectrum / NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History I, Ch 2

questions.q: The Diwan-i-Mustakhraj, a department set up to collect arrears of revenue, is associated with which one of the following rulers?
questions.e: Alauddin Khalji set it up as part of his revenue and market reforms to recover arrears from the officials. Balban is linked with Diwan-i-Arz (military), and Firoz Shah Tughlaq with Diwan-i-Khairat (charity).
questions.s: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Spectrum Medieval notes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mansabdari system under the Mughals:
1. The zat of a mansabdar indicated his personal rank and salary.
2. The sawar rank indicated the number of horsemen he was required to maintain.
3. The system was introduced by Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar, not Shah Jahan. Zat and sawar together fixed a mansabdar's status and his contingent obligations.

questions.q: Which one of the following temples is NOT correctly matched with the dynasty that built it?
questions.e: Khajuraho's Kandariya Mahadeva is a Nagara-style temple of the Chandelas, not the Palas. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture, Ch 'Temple Architecture'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti is located in Delhi.
2. Verses of Baba Farid are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
3. The Suhrawardi silsila in India was introduced by Moinuddin Chishti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Moinuddin Chishti's dargah is in Ajmer, and the Suhrawardi order spread through Bahauddin Zakariya of Multan, so statements 1 and 3 are wrong. Baba Farid's verses entered the Adi Granth compiled by Guru Arjan Dev.

questions.q: The Gutenberg discontinuity separates which of the following layers of the Earth?
questions.e: Gutenberg lies at about 2,900 km depth, where P-waves slow and S-waves vanish at the liquid outer core. Moho separates crust and mantle and Lehmann separates outer and inner core.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 3

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of parent rock and metamorphic rock is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Sandstone changes to quartzite, while slate forms from shale or clay. The other pairs are standard.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: In the stratosphere, temperature increases with height.
Statement-II: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Ozone absorbs UV and converts it to heat, so the stratosphere warms upward, which is a direct cause-effect link. This warm layer sits above the cold tropopause and resists vertical mixing.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Coriolis force deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.
2. The Coriolis force is maximum at the equator.
3. A geostrophic wind blows parallel to the isobars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and increases towards the poles. When it balances the pressure gradient force, wind flows parallel to the isobars as a geostrophic wind.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 9

questions.q: Which one of the following is the highest peak in India south of the Himalayas?
questions.e: Anamudi (about 2,695 m) in the Western Ghats of Kerala is the highest peak of peninsular India. Doddabetta is the Nilgiris' highest, Mahendragiri is in the Eastern Ghats, and Dhupgarh is the Satpura range's highest.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of rivers flows into the Arabian Sea through estuaries rather than deltas?
questions.e: Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys over hard rock and carry little silt, so they form estuaries. Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi and Cauvery all form deltas on the east coast, and Mahanadi drains to the Bay of Bengal.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Western Disturbances:
1. They bring winter rainfall to north-western India.
2. They are associated with the subtropical westerly jet stream.
3. The rain they bring is mainly beneficial to the kharif crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Western Disturbances are extra-tropical cyclonic systems from the Mediterranean region steered eastward by the westerly jet. Their winter rain suits rabi crops such as wheat, not kharif crops.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Net National Product is obtained by adding depreciation to Gross National Product.
2. Gross National Product is equal to Gross Domestic Product plus net factor income from abroad.
3. National Income is Net National Product at factor cost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NNP is GNP minus depreciation, so statement 1 is wrong. National Income is NNP at factor cost, which is the total income earned by factors of production.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'National Income'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.
2. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit plus interest payments.
3. Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts.
4. Effective revenue deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments, so it shows the gap excluding past debt burden. The other definitions are correct.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'Public Finance'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The framework for flexible inflation targeting was given a statutory basis through an amendment to the RBI Act, 1934 in 2016.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee has six members, and the Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie.
3. The inflation target is fixed by the RBI alone, without involving the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The target is notified by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI, so statement 3 is wrong. The MPC has three RBI members and three external members appointed by the Centre.

questions.q:
Statement-I: An increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio reduces the lending capacity of commercial banks.
Statement-II: CRR is the share of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be held with the RBI.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A higher CRR locks more bank funds with the RBI, so less is left to lend. That is why the RBI raises CRR to drain liquidity and curb inflation.

questions.q:
Which of the following items are recorded in the current account of India's balance of payments?
1. Personal remittances from abroad
2. Foreign direct investment inflows
3. Interest income on external debt
4. Exports and imports of services
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: FDI is a capital account (financial account) item. Remittances (secondary income), interest and investment income (primary income) and services trade are all current account items.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'External Sector'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rabi crops are sown in October to December and harvested in April to June.
2. Cotton is a rabi crop.
3. Zaid crops are grown in the summer months between the rabi and kharif seasons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cotton is a kharif crop sown with the monsoon. Watermelon, muskmelon and cucumber are typical zaid crops.

questions.q: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), which emphasised rapid industrialisation with priority to heavy industries, was based on the model of:
questions.e: The Second Plan used Mahalanobis's model of a capital goods sector driving growth. The First Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar approach.

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, loans to micro-enterprises are classified into categories. Which one of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.e: The scheme names its loan bands Shishu, Kishor and Tarun, with Tarun Plus added later. 'Yuva' is not a PMMY category.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ecological pyramids:
1. The pyramid of energy is always upright.
2. The pyramid of biomass in an ocean ecosystem can be inverted.
3. The pyramid of numbers in a tree ecosystem can be inverted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Energy is lost as heat at each trophic level, so the energy pyramid is never inverted. In oceans, tiny phytoplankton reproduce fast, so their biomass at a moment is smaller than the zooplankton they support, and a single tree supports many insects.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT part of a biodiversity hotspot that includes territory of India?
questions.e: India's hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). Eastern Ghats is not a recognised hotspot.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Project Tiger was launched in 1973.
2. The National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. Project Elephant was launched in 1973 along with Project Tiger.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Project Elephant began in 1992. The NTCA got statutory status through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority, set up under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002?
questions.e: The NBA is headquartered in Chennai. It works with State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the Montreux Record?
o: It lists all wetlands newly designated as Ramsar sites each year
It is a register of Ramsar sites where the ecological character has changed, is changing or is likely to change due to human interference
It is a register of species placed under Appendix I of CITES
It is a list of protected areas threatened by climate change maintained by IUCN
questions.e: The Montreux Record is maintained under the Ramsar Convention to flag sites needing priority attention. Loktak Lake in Manipur is an Indian site that has been on it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kyoto Protocol set legally binding emission reduction targets for developed countries.
2. Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement are legally binding targets backed by penalties.
3. The Paris Agreement entered into force in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Paris the process obligations (submitting and reporting NDCs) are binding, but the NDC targets themselves are nationally determined and carry no penalties. It entered into force on 4 November 2016.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a secondary air pollutant?
questions.e: Ground-level ozone is not emitted directly but forms when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight. CO, SO2 and dust are emitted directly as primary pollutants.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's Mars Orbiter Mission entered Mars orbit in its first attempt.
2. The Mars Orbiter Mission was launched by a GSLV rocket.
3. Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south polar region in August 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Mars Orbiter Mission was launched on a PSLV, not a GSLV, and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014. Chandrayaan-3's lander touched down on 23 August 2023.

questions.q: Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory mission, was placed in which one of the following orbits?
o: A halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point L1
A geostationary orbit around the Earth
A polar orbit around the Sun
A halo orbit around the Earth-Moon L2 point
questions.e: Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 in September 2023 and reached its halo orbit around L1 in January 2024. From L1 it views the Sun continuously without eclipses.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about India's three-stage nuclear power programme?
o: The first stage uses fast breeder reactors
The third stage uses Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors with natural uranium
The second stage uses fast breeder reactors with plutonium-based fuel
The programme was designed mainly to use uranium-235 enrichment
questions.e: Stage one uses PHWRs with natural uranium, stage two uses fast breeder reactors with plutonium recovered from stage one, and stage three uses thorium with uranium-233. The design reflects India's large thorium reserves.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about hydrogen production:
1. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using renewable energy.
2. Grey hydrogen is produced from natural gas through steam methane reforming.
3. Brown hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using nuclear energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Brown hydrogen comes from coal (lignite), while hydrogen from nuclear-powered electrolysis is called pink hydrogen. Grey hydrogen emits CO2 because no carbon capture is used.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of vitamin and deficiency disease is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, while beriberi results from thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency.
questions.s: NCERT Class VIII Science / Class IX Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A patent in India is granted for a term of 20 years from the date of filing.
2. Copyright in a literary work in India generally lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years.
3. Registration of copyright is compulsory for the copyright to exist.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Copyright arises automatically on creation, and registration is only evidence of ownership. The patent term runs from the filing date, not the grant date.
